title: Book Six (1808 - 10) — Chapter 22
paragraphs: In 1809, the intimacy between "the world's two arbiters," as Napoleon and Alexander were called, had become so close that when Napoleon declared war on Austria, a Russian corps crossed the frontier to fight alongside their old enemy Bonaparte against their old ally the Austrian Emperor, and at court people even spoke of a possible marriage between Napoleon and one of Alexander's sisters. But besides foreign policy, Russian society's attention was keenly focused on the internal reforms being carried out across all branches of government.

Life, meanwhile — real life, with its essential concerns of health and sickness, work and rest, and its intellectual pursuits of thought, science, poetry, music, love, friendship, hatred, and passion — went on as usual, independently of and apart from political friendship or enmity with Napoleon Bonaparte, and from all the grand schemes of reform.
